subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on two-stage subagent inactivity recovery, and what activity source, thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, parent wake contract, and channel notification behavior should it use?
rationale: The remaining work adds recovery policy, config/default behavior, mutating child-run control, and channel/user-visible failure handling for existing deployments, so automation cannot safely choose it as a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Define core recovery policy
options.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity plus kill/reap items.

options.title: Prototype default-off
options.body: Allow an experimental opt-in watchdog first, with focused live proof and no behavior change for existing installs until defaults are accepted.

options.title: Defer to narrower controls
options.body: Rely on runTimeoutSeconds plus future manual kill/reap and session-activity surfaces, then revisit automatic escalation with more production evidence.

recommendation.title: Define core recovery policy
recommendation.body: Adopt the feature only after maintainers specify the default or opt-in stance, activity signal, nudge and kill semantics, parent wake contract, channel notification wording, and relationship to session activity plus kill/reap items.

likelyOwner.reason: Existing review context and subagent registry/control history point to steipete as the strongest owner for choosing recovery semantics.
